sessions.setting: Their shared apartment, Friday evening after classes

turns.speaker: alice
turns.text: Hey, you're home early! I thought you had band practice tonight.

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: Nah, The Wavelengths canceled rehearsal. Jake's got the flu. So I stopped by the pet store on the way back.

turns.speaker: alice
turns.text: Oh no, what did you do.

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: So, don't be mad... I got a goldfish. His name is Beethoven.

turns.speaker: alice
turns.text: Bob. We've been roommates for what, four years now? And you just bring home a fish without asking?

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: Hey, you brought Mochi home without exactly running it by me first! I came back from class and there was just... a cat on the couch.

turns.speaker: alice
turns.text: That's different! I adopted Mochi from the shelter. That was a rescue situation. She needed a home.

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: And Beethoven needed a home too. He was the last one in the tank. He looked lonely.

turns.speaker: alice
turns.text: You are so dramatic. Fine. Where are you going to put him?

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: I was thinking on the bookshelf by the window? The light's good there.

turns.speaker: alice
turns.text: Just keep him away from Mochi. She's been staring at the fish tank at the vet's office every time we go. I don't trust her.

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: Noted. Beethoven will be safe. I promise.

sessions.setting: Their shared apartment, late evening, Alice studying at the kitchen table

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: Still working on that Rust project?

turns.speaker: alice
turns.text: Yeah, Rust is honestly the best language for what I'm building. The memory safety guarantees save me so much debugging time.

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: I don't know how you stare at code all day. I'd lose my mind.

turns.speaker: alice
turns.text: Says the guy who spent six hours yesterday scoring a thirty-second scene transition.

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: That's different! Film scoring is an art. I was going for a Hans Zimmer thing, that layered tension he does. It's harder than it sounds.

turns.speaker: alice
turns.text: I know, I know. Hey, do you remember that hackathon I did last November? The sign-language recognition app?

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: The one that won first place? Yeah, obviously. You didn't sleep for like two days.

turns.speaker: alice
turns.text: So the faculty advisor just emailed me about turning it into a proper research project. But my wrist is still bothering me from that bouldering fall last month. Typing for hours is rough.

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: Wait, I thought the cast came off and you were fine?

turns.speaker: alice
turns.text: The cast is off, but it still aches when I type too long. Six weeks in a cast doesn't mean everything's magically healed. I'm doing physical therapy.

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: That sucks. Maybe you should get one of those ergonomic keyboards?

turns.speaker: alice
turns.text: Already ordered one. Should be here Monday.

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: Nice. Well, I'm going to go work on my composition homework. Professor wants us to analyze a full orchestral score by Wednesday.

turns.speaker: alice
turns.text: Good luck with that. Don't stay up too late.

sessions.setting: Their shared apartment, Tuesday morning getting ready for the day

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: I'm heading out. Got the early shift at Crema today.

turns.speaker: alice
turns.text: On a Tuesday? That's rough.

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: Yeah, I swapped shifts because Sofia's visiting this weekend. My little sister's looking at schools up here.

turns.speaker: alice
turns.text: Oh that's exciting! She's graduating high school this year, right?

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: Next year, but she wants to do campus tours early. I told her she'd love it here.

turns.speaker: alice
turns.text: She should totally come check it out. Hey, remind me to call my parents tonight? They want to talk about Golden Dragon stuff. Something about expanding the lunch menu.

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: Your parents' restaurant always has the best food. I miss those dumplings from when we visited Portland over spring break freshman year.

turns.speaker: alice
turns.text: I'll tell my mom. She'll send a care package again. Oh, and I can't do dinner tomorrow night. I've got the coding workshop for the high schoolers.

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: That's every Saturday, right?

turns.speaker: alice
turns.text: Every Saturday, yeah. But tomorrow a few of us mentors are meeting to plan the curriculum for next quarter. I really love it though. Reminds me of growing up in Portland, when there wasn't much tech stuff available for kids like that.

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: That's cool. Alright, I really gotta run or I'll be late. See you tonight?

turns.speaker: alice
turns.text: Yep, I'll be here. Have a good shift!

sessions.setting: Their shared apartment, Alice packing gear in the living room

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: Are you seriously going climbing this weekend? Your wrist just healed.

turns.speaker: alice
turns.text: I've been climbing since I was fourteen. I know my limits. I'm doing easy routes only, nothing above a 5.8.

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: That's what you said last time, and then you came home in a cast.

turns.speaker: alice
turns.text: That was bouldering, totally different. Anyway, I need to stay active. I signed up for that half-marathon in October, remember? I should be cross-training.

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: A half-marathon? When did that happen?

turns.speaker: alice
turns.text: I told you last week! You were probably zoning out at the piano again.

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: Hey, I can multitask. I play piano, drums, AND bass guitar. My brain's always doing three things at once.

turns.speaker: alice
turns.text: And yet you can't remember a conversation from five days ago. Impressive.

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: Fair point. Speaking of running, I actually ran that 10K charity race last month. The one for music education?

turns.speaker: alice
turns.text: Oh right! How was that?

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: Brutal. I am not a runner. But we raised like three grand, so it was worth it.

turns.speaker: alice
turns.text: Nice. Okay, I'm loading up the Civic. Want anything from the outdoor store? I'm stopping on the way.

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: Nah, I'm good. Just don't break anything this time, please.

turns.speaker: alice
turns.text: I'll do my best. See you Sunday night.

sessions.setting: Outdoor cafe near campus, Saturday lunch date

turns.speaker: carol
turns.text: Sorry I'm late. I did my morning run and then completely lost track of time reviewing my global health notes.

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: No worries. I ordered you a coffee already. And I made you something special at work this morning to bring along.

turns.speaker: carol
turns.text: Aw, what is it?

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: A cortado. It's my favorite drink to make. Got the foam art just right on this one. Well, it was perfect an hour ago. It's probably cold now.

turns.speaker: carol
turns.text: I love that you always do that. How long has it been since the jazz festival? When we first met?

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: Last June, so almost a year. Best night of my life. I saw you standing by the stage and I just knew.

turns.speaker: carol
turns.text: You literally spilled a drink on my jacket. That's what happened.

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: And then I offered to get it dry cleaned, and THAT turned into coffee, and HERE we are.

turns.speaker: carol
turns.text: Here we are. So, I've been meaning to tell you. I've been thinking a lot about my pre-med path lately. There's so much I want to do in global health, but the workload is crushing.

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: You're doing amazing though. With the clinic and everything.

turns.speaker: carol
turns.text: Thanks. It helps that I run every morning. Those five kilometers at 6 AM keep me sane. Clears my head before the chaos starts.

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: 6 AM. I genuinely do not understand morning people.

turns.speaker: carol
turns.text: And I don't understand people who stay up until 3 AM composing music, so we're even.

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: Touche.

sessions.setting: Bob's apartment, cooking dinner together

turns.speaker: carol
turns.text: Okay, the kimchi jjigae is almost done. My mom's recipe. She'd be so proud that I'm actually making this instead of ordering takeout.

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: It smells incredible. My cooking skills max out at scrambled eggs, so this is a real treat.

turns.speaker: carol
turns.text: Kimchi jjigae is literally my favorite thing in the world. My mom makes the best version. Every time I go home to Seattle I eat it three days in a row.

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: We should go visit your family sometime. I still haven't met them.

turns.speaker: carol
turns.text: Mm, we will. Daniel called me today, actually. My little brother. He's adjusting to college life. Keeps asking for study advice. Anyway, how was your week? You mentioned the film scoring thing?

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: Yeah! So you know that student short film I scored last semester? The one that won the regional award?

turns.speaker: carol
turns.text: The one you were so nervous about? Of course!

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: The director just told me she's submitting it to a national festival. And she wants me to compose a new piece for her next project.

turns.speaker: carol
turns.text: Bob, that's amazing! I'm so proud of you.

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: Thanks. It really makes me feel like Vienna was worth it. That film music workshop last summer changed how I think about scoring.

turns.speaker: carol
turns.text: I remember you telling me about it. You came back all inspired. Like how I felt after Ghana.

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: Your medical volunteer thing? Yeah, you came back like a different person.

turns.speaker: carol
turns.text: It changed everything. Seeing healthcare in rural communities there... it's why I'm pushing so hard with pre-med. I know exactly what I want to do.

sessions.setting: Walking across campus after Carol's clinic shift

turns.speaker: carol
turns.text: Ugh, that was a long shift. Tuesdays and Thursdays at the clinic are always intense. We had a line out the door today.

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: You volunteer there twice a week on top of everything else? I don't know how you do it.

turns.speaker: carol
turns.text: It's good practice. Plus, I need the clinical hours for my med school applications. Oh, speaking of studying, I officially registered for the September MCAT. It's real now.

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: September? That's coming up fast.

turns.speaker: carol
turns.text: Don't remind me. I have a whole study plan. I'm going through Kaplan, doing practice tests every weekend. Oh, I also signed up for a conversational Spanish class to keep my language skills sharp. I want to be fluent eventually, on top of Korean and English.

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: Overachiever.

turns.speaker: carol
turns.text: Says the guy who volunteers as a music tutor on weekends AND plays in a band.

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: The tutoring is different. Those kids are incredible. There's this one girl who went from not knowing how to hold drumsticks to playing a full beat in three weeks.

turns.speaker: carol
turns.text: That's wonderful. How's band stuff going, by the way?

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: Actually, great. The Wavelengths just got invited to play at the Spring Music Festival. The big one on the quad.

turns.speaker: carol
turns.text: Are you serious? That's a huge deal! I'll be in the front row.

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: You better be. We're doing three original songs and two covers. I've been rehearsing like crazy.

turns.speaker: carol
turns.text: I wouldn't miss it. I need a break from MCAT prep anyway. Just tell me the date.

sessions.setting: University chemistry lab, after organic chemistry class

turns.speaker: carol
turns.text: Okay, I think our titration results are way off. Did you check the molarity on that solution?

turns.speaker: david
turns.text: Yeah, I recalculated it. I think the pipette was giving us inconsistent volumes. Being lab partners with you means I have to double-check everything because you'll definitely catch it.

turns.speaker: carol
turns.text: I take that as a compliment. Hey, you seem tired today. Everything okay?

turns.speaker: david
turns.text: Training's been intense. I'm trying to qualify for Boston. My Chicago Marathon time last October was three hours fifteen, and I need to shave about ten minutes off for a Boston qualifying time.

turns.speaker: carol
turns.text: That's serious. How much are you running?

turns.speaker: david
turns.text: I bumped up to 60 miles a week. It's a lot on top of coursework, but I really want this.

turns.speaker: carol
turns.text: I get it. I'm the same way with the clinic stuff. Oh, that reminds me. The blood drive I organized last month? Final numbers came in. We got 200 donations.

turns.speaker: david
turns.text: 200? That's incredible. How did you get that many people to show up?

turns.speaker: carol
turns.text: I basically harassed every student org on campus. Posters, group chats, bribery with free cookies. It worked.

turns.speaker: david
turns.text: You're terrifyingly efficient. I respect that.

turns.speaker: carol
turns.text: Thank you. Now let's figure out why our reaction yield is only 40 percent. That's not going to fly for the lab report.

turns.speaker: david
turns.text: Already on it. I think we need to adjust the temperature. Let me recalculate the activation energy.

sessions.setting: Campus cafeteria, grabbing lunch between classes

turns.speaker: david
turns.text: So I got some good news. Remember that protein folding research I've been doing?

turns.speaker: carol
turns.text: The one with Professor Henderson? Yeah!

turns.speaker: david
turns.text: I won the departmental biochemistry research award for it. They're going to present it at the end-of-year ceremony.

turns.speaker: carol
turns.text: David! That's amazing! Congratulations! Your dad must be thrilled.

turns.speaker: david
turns.text: He is. Being a pharmacology professor at the University of Chicago, he gets weirdly competitive about academic awards. He called me three times to talk about it.

turns.speaker: carol
turns.text: That's sweet though. Growing up in Chicago with a professor dad, no wonder you're so disciplined.

turns.speaker: david
turns.text: Ha, yeah. It was definitely... structured. What about you? Anything new?

turns.speaker: carol
turns.text: Well, two things. First, remember that community service award I won last spring? The university one? They want me to give a speech at orientation for incoming students.

turns.speaker: david
turns.text: You'd be great at that. What's the second thing?

turns.speaker: carol
turns.text: I adopted a hamster. From the bio department. They were rehoming the ones from the behavioral study.

turns.speaker: david
turns.text: You adopted a lab hamster?

turns.speaker: carol
turns.text: His name is Tofu, and he's perfect, and I love him already.

turns.speaker: david
turns.text: I can't judge. I have a turtle named Newton in my dorm room.

turns.speaker: carol
turns.text: Wait, Newton? How have we been lab partners all semester and I didn't know you have a pet turtle?

sessions.setting: Study room in the university library

turns.speaker: carol
turns.text: I'm so deep in MCAT prep that I forgot what it's like to read for fun. I miss actual books.

turns.speaker: david
turns.text: What would you be reading if you had time?

turns.speaker: carol
turns.text: Probably rereading 'Mountains Beyond Mountains' by Tracy Kidder. It's about Paul Farmer and his work in Haiti. It's the book that made me want to do global health in the first place.

turns.speaker: david
turns.text: I've heard of it. I should check it out. My go-to is 'The Emperor of All Maladies' by Siddhartha Mukherjee. The way he tells the history of cancer research... it's basically what got me interested in the research side of medicine.

turns.speaker: carol
turns.text: Speaking of research and medicine, how are your grad school apps going?

turns.speaker: david
turns.text: Slowly. MD-PhD programs have so many essays. I've been working on the Johns Hopkins one all week.

turns.speaker: carol
turns.text: MD-PhD is brutal to apply for. But with your research award and your GPA, you'll be fine.

turns.speaker: david
turns.text: I hope so. I've been stressed about it. Newton can tell. He's been hiding in his shell more than usual.

turns.speaker: carol
turns.text: Your turtle is an emotional barometer now?

turns.speaker: david
turns.text: Turtles are more perceptive than people give them credit for. How's Tofu doing?

turns.speaker: carol
turns.text: He's great. He runs on his wheel at 3 AM like clockwork. It's strangely comforting. Reminds me why I do this. All the work, the MCAT, the applications. Someday I want to be like Paul Farmer. Work with Doctors Without Borders after med school. Go where help is needed most.

turns.speaker: david
turns.text: That's a good north star to have. We'll both get there.

turns.speaker: carol
turns.text: We will. Okay, back to organic chemistry mechanisms. Page 247.

sessions.setting: Campus tutoring center, during a break between sessions

turns.speaker: eve
turns.text: That calc student was tough today. She kept mixing up integration by parts and substitution.

turns.speaker: david
turns.text: I noticed. You were really patient with her though. Working together at this tutoring center has made me realize I don't have your patience.

turns.speaker: eve
turns.text: You're plenty patient! You just have a more... direct teaching style. Which some students actually prefer.

turns.speaker: david
turns.text: Direct is a nice way to put it. Hey, are you free Saturday morning? I've got my youth track coaching, but after that I was going to grab lunch.

turns.speaker: eve
turns.text: I can't Saturday. I've got zero-waste week planning. Being the campus sustainability coordinator is basically a second job right now. We're trying to get every dining hall to switch to compostable containers.

turns.speaker: david
turns.text: That sounds like a nightmare of bureaucracy.

turns.speaker: eve
turns.text: It is. But I got the university president to agree to a meeting, so that's progress. It ties into my thesis too.

turns.speaker: david
turns.text: What's your thesis on again?

turns.speaker: eve
turns.text: Urban composting systems. Specifically how university campuses can implement closed-loop food waste programs. I've been collecting data from our campus compost bins for six months.

turns.speaker: david
turns.text: That's really cool. I wish I could find that kind of overlap between my work and extracurriculars. My running coaching is fun, but the kids on the youth track program don't exactly connect to protein folding research.

turns.speaker: eve
turns.text: You never know. Maybe one of them will become a biochemist who runs marathons. You'd be their origin story.

turns.speaker: david
turns.text: Ha. I like that. Alright, my 3 PM tutee is here. Back to work.

sessions.setting: Campus green, eating lunch on a bench

turns.speaker: eve
turns.text: What did you bring for lunch? That smells amazing.

turns.speaker: david
turns.text: Jollof rice. My grandmother's recipe. I taught myself to cook Nigerian dishes during my first semester here. I was so homesick, and cooking her food was the only thing that helped.

turns.speaker: eve
turns.text: That's really sweet. I get the comfort food thing. I do the same with Thai food. I'm vegetarian, so finding good options on campus is hard. I just make my own pad thai and curries at home.

turns.speaker: david
turns.text: You should bring some next time. I'll trade you jollof rice for pad thai.

turns.speaker: eve
turns.text: Deal. Maple would also appreciate any leftovers. She's been spoiled lately.

turns.speaker: david
turns.text: Maple?

turns.speaker: eve
turns.text: My dog! I adopted her during sophomore year from a rescue. She's this scruffy little terrier mix with one ear that never stands up straight. She's the best.

turns.speaker: david
turns.text: I didn't know you had a dog. Newton is going to be jealous. He's my only companion in the dorm.

turns.speaker: eve
turns.text: You should bring Newton over sometime. Maple is very gentle with small creatures. Mostly.

turns.speaker: david
turns.text: I'll pass on that risk. Hey, did I tell you about my trip to Lagos last summer?

turns.speaker: eve
turns.text: No! How was it?

turns.speaker: david
turns.text: Incredible. I visited my extended family. My cousins took me to all these places I remembered from when I was a kid. And the food... my grandmother made jollof rice every single day I was there. I took so many notes on her technique.

turns.speaker: eve
turns.text: That sounds like such a meaningful trip. I love when food connects you to your roots like that.

sessions.setting: Tutoring center, end of shift

turns.speaker: david
turns.text: Hey, before we leave, I wanted to ask you something. You do a lot of campus organizing, right? I'm trying to put together a 5K fundraiser for sickle cell research and I could use some advice.

turns.speaker: eve
turns.text: Oh, absolutely! I just went through a whole grant-writing process for my campus garden project. Got EPA funding for it, actually. So I know the bureaucratic maze pretty well now.

turns.speaker: david
turns.text: You got an EPA grant? That's legit.

turns.speaker: eve
turns.text: Took months of paperwork, but yeah. The garden is going to have 30 beds for students to grow their own produce. Anyway, for your 5K, what's your timeline?

turns.speaker: david
turns.text: I'm thinking early fall. I already have a route mapped out around campus. I just need help with permits and sponsors.

turns.speaker: eve
turns.text: I can help with that. Forward me your plan and I'll mark it up. Oh, what's that thing on your desk? Is that new?

turns.speaker: david
turns.text: The standing desk? I built it myself. From reclaimed wood. Found some old shelving that the maintenance department was throwing out and converted it.

turns.speaker: eve
turns.text: You built a standing desk from reclaimed wood? Okay, that's very on-brand for me. I'm impressed.

turns.speaker: david
turns.text: Ha, I figured you'd appreciate the sustainability angle. What have you been up to outside of tutoring?

turns.speaker: eve
turns.text: I've been painting a lot. Watercolor landscapes, mostly. I'm getting ready for the campus art fair next month. I actually sell them there.

turns.speaker: david
turns.text: Wait, you sell your paintings?

turns.speaker: eve
turns.text: Yeah! It helps pay for Maple's vet bills. I also picked up the ukulele again. I'm doing an open mic night this Thursday if you want to come.

turns.speaker: david
turns.text: A ukulele open mic night. Sure, why not. I'll be there.

sessions.setting: Coffee shop off campus, catching up over lattes

turns.speaker: alice
turns.text: I can't believe it's been seven years since that coding camp. We were fifteen! Remember how we both almost quit the first day?

turns.speaker: eve
turns.text: Oh my god, yes. The instructor was so intimidating. And then you helped me debug my first Python script and we've been friends ever since.

turns.speaker: alice
turns.text: Portland kids sticking together. I miss home sometimes.

turns.speaker: eve
turns.text: Same. Growing up in the same neighborhood as you was the best. Do you remember that huge oak tree in the park between our streets?

turns.speaker: alice
turns.text: The one we used to climb? Of course. Hey, so I made xiaolongbao from scratch last weekend. My grandmother's recipe. Took me four hours and they were... okay.

turns.speaker: eve
turns.text: Your grandmother's xiaolongbao were legendary. Your grandma is a culinary genius.

turns.speaker: alice
turns.text: She really is. She'd be disappointed in my soup dumplings though. The folds were all wrong. I'll keep practicing.

turns.speaker: eve
turns.text: Bring some next time and I'll be your taste tester. What else is new? How was winter break?

turns.speaker: alice
turns.text: Amazing, actually. My family went to Tokyo. It was my first time there. The food, the architecture, everything was incredible. My dad cried at a ramen shop because it reminded him of his childhood.

turns.speaker: eve
turns.text: That's so sweet. I spent winter break back in Portland with my parents. My mom had a new landscaping project she wanted to show me. You know how she is with her designs.

turns.speaker: alice
turns.text: Your mom's landscape architecture is always beautiful. Remember that garden she did for the community center?

turns.speaker: eve
turns.text: She still talks about that one. It's her favorite project. We should both go back to Portland soon and do a proper visit.

sessions.setting: Alice's apartment, Eve visiting with Maple

turns.speaker: eve
turns.text: Maple, no! Don't chase Mochi! Sorry, she'll calm down in a second.

turns.speaker: alice
turns.text: It's fine. Mochi's hiding under the bed. She'll come out when she's ready. Want some tea?

turns.speaker: eve
turns.text: Please. So tell me about the grad school stuff. You mentioned you were looking into HCI programs?

turns.speaker: alice
turns.text: Yeah, I'm applying to graduate programs in human-computer interaction. Carnegie Mellon, Georgia Tech, UW. The application deadlines are in December so I'm trying to get my portfolio together.

turns.speaker: eve
turns.text: That's exciting! You'll get in somewhere great. Have you been reading anything for inspiration?

turns.speaker: alice
turns.text: I've been rereading 'The Design of Everyday Things' by Don Norman. It's my favorite book. Every time I read it I notice something new about how people interact with technology.

turns.speaker: eve
turns.text: I should borrow that. I've been so deep in ecology papers that I forgot other subjects exist. My semester abroad in Costa Rica studying tropical ecology kind of ruined me for anything that isn't environmental science.

turns.speaker: alice
turns.text: You loved Costa Rica so much. I remember your emails were like nature documentaries.

turns.speaker: eve
turns.text: It was transformative. I saw cloud forests and sustainable coffee farms and... ugh, I want to go back so badly. But for now, I'm getting my nature fix on trails around here. Though nothing compares to Eagle Creek Trail back in Portland. That's still my all-time favorite hike.

turns.speaker: alice
turns.text: We should hike Eagle Creek when we're home for Thanksgiving. Hey, do you want to hear something? I've been practicing a new song.

turns.speaker: eve
turns.text: On the guitar? Yes, always!

turns.speaker: alice
turns.text: Let me grab it. I've been playing so much lately. It's my stress relief from applications. My grandfather would be proud. He's the one who taught me acoustic guitar when I was a kid.

turns.speaker: eve
turns.text: I remember him playing at your family dinners. He was so good. Play me what you've got.

sessions.setting: Behind the counter at Crema Coffee, early morning shift together

turns.speaker: david
turns.text: You look like you barely slept.

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: I was up until 2 AM working on a composition. But here I am, being a responsible barista at Crema Coffee.

turns.speaker: david
turns.text: Meanwhile I've already run 10K this morning. Got up at 5:30 like always. My morning run is non-negotiable.

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: You are not human. How do you run before the sun's even up and then come here and make espresso like it's nothing?

turns.speaker: david
turns.text: Discipline. Speaking of which, you've got milk foam on your tattoo.

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: What? Oh. My treble clef tattoo is forever getting dirty at this job. Occupational hazard of having it on my wrist.

turns.speaker: david
turns.text: Why'd you get it on your wrist of all places?

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: Because music is my pulse, man. Also I was eighteen and thought it would be cool. Anyway, slow morning. I've been looking up vintage keyboards during downtime. I'm saving up for a Fender Rhodes.

turns.speaker: david
turns.text: How much does one of those run?

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: Good ones go for like two to three thousand. So at barista wages, I should have enough by... 2030.

turns.speaker: david
turns.text: Ha. Well, every shift helps. I'm mostly here for the free coffee and the schedule flexibility. It works with my training schedule.

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: Yeah, working at the same coffee shop definitely has its perks. At least we suffer through the early shifts together.

turns.speaker: david
turns.text: Alright, rush is about to start. You take register, I'll do drinks.

sessions.setting: Crema Coffee, during a slow afternoon shift

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: Hey, can I ask you something? You ever think about going back to where you grew up? Long-term, I mean.

turns.speaker: david
turns.text: Chicago? Sometimes. I miss my family. Why, are you thinking about San Diego?

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: A little. My mom keeps asking when I'm coming home. She's a music teacher at a high school in San Diego, and she keeps saying there are jobs for me there. But I've been looking into Berklee for a master's degree.

turns.speaker: david
turns.text: Berklee College of Music? That's in Boston, right? That's far from San Diego.

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: Very far. But it's one of the best for composition. I just don't know if I'm ready to commit to that yet.

turns.speaker: david
turns.text: I get it. I'm dealing with the same thing with my MD-PhD apps. Some of these programs are across the country. But we go where the opportunity is, right?

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: Right. How's your car holding up, by the way? I saw you got a parking ticket last week.

turns.speaker: david
turns.text: The Corolla's fine. That red thing is a magnet for parking enforcement apparently. I need to just start biking. You don't have a car, do you?

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: Nah, I take the bus or bum rides off Alice. Hey, random question. How many languages do you speak?

turns.speaker: david
turns.text: English, Igbo from my parents, and I took French in high school. I can get by. Why?

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: Carol's learning Spanish on top of Korean and English. Seems like everyone around me is multilingual and I can barely handle English.

turns.speaker: david
turns.text: You speak the universal language of music, man. That counts.

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: Smooth. Very smooth.

sessions.setting: Pottery studio on campus, working at adjacent wheels

turns.speaker: eve
turns.text: I can't believe we're back in the pottery studio. Last semester's class was so much fun.

turns.speaker: carol
turns.text: I know! Taking that pottery class with you was the best decision. Even though my vases all looked like sad mushrooms.

turns.speaker: eve
turns.text: They had character! I still have the mug you made me. I use it every day.

turns.speaker: carol
turns.text: You're sweet. I miss having a creative outlet. Ballet on Wednesday evenings helps, but it's more about stress relief than making something tangible.

turns.speaker: eve
turns.text: You do ballet? I didn't know that!

turns.speaker: carol
turns.text: Just a class. Nothing serious. It keeps me flexible and gets my mind off the MCAT. I picked it up the same way I picked up knitting during the pandemic. I taught myself to knit and started making scarves for the homeless shelter. I just need to do something with my hands.

turns.speaker: eve
turns.text: That's really lovely. The scarves thing. Hey, speaking of hands-on crafts, I did a workshop last month on making beeswax food wraps. You should come to the next one.

turns.speaker: carol
turns.text: Oh, that sounds fun. Are those the reusable ones that replace plastic wrap?

turns.speaker: eve
turns.text: Exactly. It's part of our campus sustainability push. My mom actually gave me the idea. She uses them in her work all the time. Being a landscape architect, she's always thinking about eco-friendly materials.

turns.speaker: carol
turns.text: That's cool that sustainability runs in your family. Okay, my bowl is collapsing. Help.

turns.speaker: eve
turns.text: You're pressing too hard. Gentle hands. Let the clay guide you.

turns.speaker: carol
turns.text: Gentle hands. Right. I'm a pre-med student who spends half her life pipetting chemicals and the other half kneading dough. My hands only know two modes: precise and aggressive.

turns.speaker: eve
turns.text: We'll work on that.

sessions.setting: Campus dining hall, Saturday lunch

turns.speaker: alice
turns.text: I can't stay too long. I have the coding workshop this afternoon and then I need to prep for a meeting at AutoMind on Monday. The internship is getting intense.

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: How's the robotics startup treating you?

turns.speaker: alice
turns.text: It's amazing. The work is hard but I'm learning so much about embedded systems. It's making me even more sure about grad school.

turns.speaker: carol
turns.text: That's awesome. Bob told me you're also planning a bake sale?

turns.speaker: alice
turns.text: Yeah! I'm organizing a fundraiser bake sale for the animal shelter where I adopted Mochi. They're running low on supplies and I figured we could help. You should both come.

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: I'll make my famous banana bread. And by famous I mean the only thing I can bake without burning it.

turns.speaker: carol
turns.text: I can bring pastries. My parents own a bakery in Seattle, Kim's Pastries. I'll call them for recipes. Maybe their signature cream puffs.

turns.speaker: alice
turns.text: Carol, that would be amazing. Your parents' bakery stuff is always incredible.

turns.speaker: carol
turns.text: Growing up in Seattle surrounded by pastries definitely gave me high standards for baked goods. Oh, also, I've been wanting to talk to you both. I'm planning a study group trip to South Korea next winter break. Would either of you want to come?

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: Korea? Absolutely. I've always wanted to go. The music scene there is incredible. And as a film scoring student, I'd love to check out the Korean cinema culture.

turns.speaker: alice
turns.text: I'd love to but it depends on grad school interviews. Tentatively yes! Oh, and I'm thinking of going to Smith Rock over fall break. Central Oregon. It's my favorite climbing route ever.

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: The climbing spot? That sounds awesome.

turns.speaker: carol
turns.text: That sounds incredible. I wish I had time for a trip like that. The MCAT is literally consuming my life.

turns.speaker: alice
turns.text: You've got this, Carol. September will be over before you know it.

sessions.setting: Bob's apartment, casual Friday evening hangout

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: Thanks for coming over. I've been stuck in film scoring homework all week and I needed human interaction.

turns.speaker: eve
turns.text: Happy to be here. I drove Cloud over and almost didn't find parking. My white Prius blends in with every other car in the lot.

turns.speaker: david
turns.text: You named your car Cloud?

turns.speaker: eve
turns.text: She's white and she glides silently. It fits. So Bob, how's Beethoven? Sofia still obsessed with him?

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: Thriving. And yeah, my little sister was practically glued to the fish tank when she visited. She wants a goldfish now too. My mom is not pleased.

turns.speaker: david
turns.text: My dad would say pets build character. Then again, he's a pharmacology professor, so everything is a learning opportunity to him.

turns.speaker: eve
turns.text: Ha. Hey, so I've been thinking a lot about post-graduation. I'm seriously considering applying for the Peace Corps. Environmental education programs.

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: Peace Corps? That's a big move.

turns.speaker: eve
turns.text: It is. But volunteering at the community garden near campus every Sunday has made me realize I want to do this work on a bigger scale. And I've been rereading 'Braiding Sweetgrass' by Robin Wall Kimmerer, my favorite book, and it just reinforces everything I feel about connecting people to the land.

turns.speaker: david
turns.text: That sounds meaningful. I respect that. What does your family think?

turns.speaker: eve
turns.text: My mom's supportive. My dad... he'd rather I take over his bookstore. He owns Park's Pages in Portland. But he understands.

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: A bookstore in Portland? That's cool. I should actually read more. I just listen to music instead.

turns.speaker: david
turns.text: Music is not reading, Bob.

turns.speaker: bob
turns.text: Everyone keeps telling me that. Fine. Eve, get me a recommendation from your dad's shop. But keep it short.
